claim: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity and hepatotoxicity are major causes of drug attrition.
source: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity and hepatotoxicity are major causes of drug attrition.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that establishes the context for the study.

claim: The study screened a library of 1280 bioactive compounds using iPSC-CMs and deep learning.
source: We screened a library of 1280 bioactive compounds and identified those with potential cardiotoxic liabilities in iPSC-CMs using a single-parameter score based on deep learning.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the experimental design and number of compounds screened.

claim: Compounds demonstrating cardiotoxicity in iPSC-CMs included DNA intercalators, ion channel blockers, EGFR inhibitors, CDK inhibitors, and multi-kinase inhibitors.
source: Compounds demonstrating cardiotoxicity in iPSC-CMs included DNA intercalators, ion channel blockers, epidermal growth factor receptor, cyclin-dependent kinase, and multi-kinase inhibitors.
evidence: The abstract explicitly lists the classes of compounds identified as cardiotoxic.

claim: Drug development requires an estimated 10 years and $0.8–2.6 billion.
source: Drug development is a lengthy and expensive endeavor, often requiring an estimated 10 years and $0.8–2.6 billion. The cost—and risk—grows exponentially as drugs advance toward the clinic (DiMasi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to DiMasi et al., 2016.

claim: Cardiotoxicity accounts for approximately one-third of drugs withdrawn due to safety concerns.
source: Cardiotoxicity alone accounts for approximately one-third of drugs withdrawn due to safety concerns (Guo et al., 2011; Mathur et al., 2013; Weaver and Valentin, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by three citations.

claim: Cells derived from iPSCs more closely recapitulate human biology than immortalized cells.
source: Cells derived from iPSCs more closely recapitulate human biology than immortalized cells (Moffat et al., 2017; Scannell and Bosley, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by two citations.

claim: iPSCs can be expanded to sufficient quantities and cultured for extended periods that facilitate screening at scale.
source: They can also be expanded to sufficient quantities and cultured for extended periods that facilitate screening at scale (Burridge et al., 2014; Ghazizadeh and Majd, 2020; Sharma et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by three citations.

claim: A plasmid containing the Bsd open reading frame was knocked into the 3′ end of the MYH6 locus of WTC iPSCs.
source: A plasmid containing the Bsd open reading frame and a selectable marker containing puromycin and green fluorescent protein was knocked into the 3′ end of the MYH6 locus of WTC iPSCs.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to generate the blasticidin-selectable iPSC line.

claim: Blasticidin selection reproducibly enriched a heterogenous population of iPSC-CMs to greater than 95% pure iPSC-CMs.
source: Following standard differentiation of iPSC-CMs (Figure 1A), blasticidin selection reproducibly enriched a heterogenous population of iPSC-CMs to greater than 95% pure iPSC-CMs as measured by ACTN2, TNNT2, and MYBPC3 immunostaining (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: 6–8 days after thaw, iPSC-CMs fully recovered and had stabilized contractility readings.
source: Then, 6–8 days after thaw, iPSC-CMs fully recovered and had stabilized contractility readings (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by contractility data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: iPSC-CMs were treated with bortezomib, doxorubicin, cisapride, sorafenib, givinostat, bafilomycin, paclitaxel, and JQ1 to establish training sets for deep learning models.
source: To establish training sets for deep learning models, we treated iPSC-CMs with bortezomib (proteasome inhibitor), doxorubicin (topoisomerase inhibitor), cisapride (serotonin 5-HT4 receptor agonist), sorafenib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor), givinostat (histone deacetylase inhibitor), bafilomycin (vacuolar-type H+-ATPase), paclitaxel (microtubule stabilizer), and JQ1 (bromodomain and extraterminal domain inhibitor) (Lamoureux et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for establishing training sets.

claim: The cardiotoxins had both a dose- and time-dependent effect on contractility measurements.
source: We observed that the cardiotoxins had both a dose- and time-dependent effect on contractility measurements.
evidence: This is supported by the heatmap data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Three levels of structural toxicity were defined: highly toxic (class 3), toxic (class 2), and mildly toxic (class 1), with DMSO-treated cells designated as non-toxic (class 0).
source: Based on contractility metrics, sarcomeric staining, and nuclear count, we define three levels of structural toxicity binned into the three categories: highly toxic (class 3), toxic (class 2), and mildly toxic (class 1). DMSO-treated cells were designated as non-toxic (class 0) (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the classification system used for training the deep learning models, supported by Figure 2F.

claim: Three deep learning models were developed: 4-class, 3-class, and 2-class.
source: Based on defined criteria for reduced contractility, loss of immunostaining, and nuclear count when cells were treated with various doses of cardiotoxins (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1), we developed three deep learning models: 4-class, 3-class, and 2-class.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the deep learning models.

claim: All three deep learning models showed more than 95% accuracy in identifying the non-toxic DMSO-treated condition.
source: All models showed more than 95% accuracy in identifying the non-toxic DMSO-treated condition (class 0).
evidence: This is supported by the accuracy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: For the 2-class model, the validation showed 100% accuracy in distinguishing the toxic from non-toxic conditions.
source: For the 2-class model, the validation showed 100% accuracy in distinguishing the toxic from non-toxic conditions.
evidence: This is supported by the accuracy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All three deep learning models showed a strong correlation (R2 > 0.93, p<0.0001) when analyzing the validation dataset.
source: The data suggested that all three models showed a strong correlation upon validation (R2 > 0.93, p<0.0001), regardless of how each deep learning model was trained (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Higher cell seeding densities lead to higher model accuracy and Z-factor.
source: We found that the higher the cell density, the higher the model accuracy and, most importantly, the higher the Z-factor.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: A minimum number of 1500 iPSC-CMs per well of a 384-well plate was required to reach a Z-factor of approximately 0.5.
source: For example, a minimum number of 1500 iPSC-CMs per well of a 384-well plate was required to reach a Z-factor of approximately 0.5, which is an acceptable level for an HCS in cell-based assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Using deep learning and the appropriate cell seeding density increases the dynamic range and reduces variability between treatment groups, increasing the Z-factor to > 0.5.
source: By using deep learning and the appropriate cell seeding density, we can increase the dynamic range and reduce the variability between treatment groups. These changes would increase the screening window coefficient (Z-factor > 0.5) for an HCS (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the Z-factor data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: All three deep learning models showed strong correlation (R2 > 0.95, p<0.0001) when applied to the screening plates.
source: Regardless of how each deep learning model was trained, all three models showed strong correlation (R2 > 0.95, p<0.0001) when applied to the screening plates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by the correlation data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The top hits showing a cardiotoxicity signal in iPSC-CMs included EGFR inhibitors, CDK1 inhibitors, DNA intercalators and synthesis inhibitors, ion channel blockers, and other multi-kinase inhibitors.
source: The top hits showing a cardiotoxicity signal in iPSC-CMs included epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors (WZ8040, AG-1478), cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) inhibitors (BI-2536, PHA-767491), DNA intercalators and synthesis inhibitors (Adrucil, daunorubicin, streptozotocin), ion channel blockers (chlorpromazine, nitrendipine), and other multi-kinase inhibitors (regorafenib).
evidence: This is supported by the screening data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Adrucil had a side effect of cardiac toxicity.
source: For example, Adrucil (DNA synthesis inhibitor) had a side effect of cardiac toxicity (RxList, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to RxList, 2020.

claim: Betamethasome was identified as a risk factor for heart failure.
source: Betamethasome (oral glucocorticoid) was identified as a risk factor for heart failure (Souverein, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Souverein, 2004.

claim: Regorafenib was linked to increased risk of cardiovascular events in patients with solid tumors.
source: Regorafenib (sorafenib analog, a multi-kinase inhibitor) was linked to increased risk of cardiovascular events in patients with solid tumors (Chen and Wang, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen and Wang, 2018.

claim: Chlorpromazine was linked to fast and irregular heart rate.
source: Chlorpromazine (dopamine and potassium channel inhibitor) was linked to fast and irregular heart rate (WebMD, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to WebMD, 2020.

claim: Daunorubicin causes cardiotoxicity.
source: Daunorubicin (doxorubicin analog, topoisomerase II inhibitor, and DNA intercalator) causes cardiotoxicity (Menna et al., 2012; Sawyer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by two citations.

claim: Rosiglitazone was associated with a significant increase in the risk of myocardial infarction.
source: Rosiglitazone (PPAR-γ agonist used to treat patients with type 2 diabetes) was associated with a significant increase in the risk of myocardial infarction (Nissen and Wolski, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nissen and Wolski, 2007.

claim: All seven validated compounds dose-dependently reduced basal respiration in iPSC-CMs.
source: Based on real-time OCR, all seven compounds dose-dependently reduced basal respiration in iPSC-CMs (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting decreased respiratory function compared to the DMSO control.
evidence: This is supported by the Seahorse data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: All seven validated compounds resulted in a dose-dependent decrease in maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity.
source: When compared to DMSO control, all compounds resulted in a dose-dependent decrease in maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity (Figure 6C, D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the Seahorse data shown in Figure 6C, D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Only PHA-767491 elevated ProBNP at all three doses.
source: Only PHA-767491 (at all three doses) elevated ProBNP.
evidence: This is supported by the ProBNP ELISA data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: WZ8040, daunorubicin, nitrendipine, and solifenacin dose-dependently reduced ProBNP.
source: In contrast, WZ8040, daunorubicin, nitrendipine, and solifenacin dose-dependently reduced ProBNP (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by the ProBNP ELISA data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Using PCA, four drugs (bortezomib, daunorubicin, doxorubicin, and BI-2536) fell into three distinct clusters, whereas the other five drugs clustered more closely with DMSO-treated controls.
source: Using PCA, four drugs (bortezomib, daunorubicin, doxorubicin, and BI-2536) fell into three distinct clusters, whereas the other five drugs (nitrendipine, PHA-767491, solifenacin, tegaserod, and WZ8040) clustered more closely with DMSO-treated controls (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Bortezomib-treated cardiomyocytes showed significant downregulation of major genes encoding structural proteins associated with different forms of familial cardiomyopathies.
source: Bortezomib-treated cardiomyocytes showed significant downregulation of major genes encoding structural proteins associated with different forms of familial cardiomyopathies (Haas et al., 2015). For example, TCAP (regulates sarcomere assembly and titin assembly; implicated in familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), MYL3 (myosin light chain 3; implicated in left ventricular hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and restrictive cardiomyopathy), LDB3, and DES were highly downregulated (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7C and a citation to Haas et al., 2015.

claim: Doxorubicin- and daunorubicin-treated clusters were identified by substantial downregulation of ANKRD1, LMNA, NKX2-5, and GATA4.
source: Doxorubicin- and daunorubicin-treated clusters were identified by substantial downregulation of ANKRD1 (associated with dilated cardiomyopathy), LMNA (Lamin A/C; known mutations result in cardiomyopathy), as well as NKX2-5,and GATA4 (two transcription factors essential for cardiac development and survival).
evidence: This is supported by the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The deep learning approach identified 33 hits from 1280 diverse compounds that cause cardiotoxicity in iPSC-CMs.
source: From the 1280 diverse compounds, our deep learning approach identified 33 hits to cause cardiotoxicity in iPSC-CMs (Figure 8A, B).
evidence: This is supported by the screening data shown in Figure 8A, B.

claim: Analysis of the structure-activity relationship revealed three structural frameworks with two compounds in each framework set.
source: Analysis of the structure-activity relationship revealed three structural frameworks with two compounds (also classified as matched pairs) in each framework set (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by the structure-activity relationship data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Adding an ethylene spacer to Framework 2a increased the cardiomyocyte toxicity score by twofold.
source: For example, Framework 2a (cardiotoxicity score: 1.41) and its matched pair Framework 2b (cardiotoxicity score: 0.69) showed that adding an ethylene spacer increased the cardiomyocyte toxicity score by twofold (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by the structure-activity relationship data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Six proteasome inhibitors showed a similar range of biochemical potencies (~12 to ~25 nM): carfilzomib, bortezomib, epoxomicin, delanzomib, ixazomib, and oprozomib.
source: We identified six inhibitors with a similar range of biochemical potencies (~12 to ~25 nM): carfilzomib, bortezomib, epoxomicin, delanzomib, ixazomib, and oprozomib.
evidence: This is supported by the biochemical potency data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Carfilzomib, bortezomib, and epoxomicin had the highest cardiotoxicity score among the six proteasome inhibitors with similar biochemical potencies.
source: Carfilzomib, bortezomib, and epoxomicin had the highest cardiotoxicity score; delanzomib showed the lowest cardiotoxicity liability; and ixazomib and oprozomib showed medium levels of cardiotoxicity (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by the cardiotoxicity score data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Delanzomib showed the lowest cardiotoxicity liability among the six proteasome inhibitors with similar biochemical potencies.
source: Carfilzomib, bortezomib, and epoxomicin had the highest cardiotoxicity score; delanzomib showed the lowest cardiotoxicity liability; and ixazomib and oprozomib showed medium levels of cardiotoxicity (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by the cardiotoxicity score data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Bortezomib and carfilzomib are FDA-approved proteasome inhibitors used for oncology indications, including multiple myeloma and mantle cell lymphoma.
source: Bortezomib and carfilzomib are FDA-approved proteasome inhibitors used for oncology indications, including multiple myeloma and mantle cell lymphoma (Dimopoulos et al., 2016; Richardson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by two citations.

claim: Patients given bortezomib and carfilzomib can develop cardiomyopathy, worsening heart rhythm, heart failure, and death due to cardiac arrest.
source: Patients given these drugs can develop cardiomyopathy, worsening heart rhythm, heart failure, and death due to cardiac arrest (Moslehi, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moslehi, 2016.

claim: iPSC-CMs cultured in TCM media showed significantly upregulated maturity markers (MYH7 and TNNI3) and downregulated neonatal myosin isoform (MYH6) compared with iPSC-CMs cultured in RPMI/LT3 media.
source: Compared to previously published protocols, recovery in culture media leads to improved maturity metrics based on quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) markers, contractility (beat rate and velocity), and immunostaining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: iPSC-CMs recovered and cultured in TCM media showed a reduced spontaneous beat rate and increased velocity of contractions.
source: Compared to previously published protocols, recovery in culture media leads to improved maturity metrics based on quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) markers, contractility (beat rate and velocity), and immunostaining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by the contractility data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: The adult human myocardium derives approximately 70–80% of its energy from oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria fueled by fatty acid–based oxidative phosphorylation.
source: The adult human myocardium is highly metabolically active. Approximately 70–80% of its energy derives from oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria fueled by fatty acid–based oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a statement about established biological knowledge.

claim: In immature neonatal myocardium or iPSC-CMs, ATP production is predominately through the glycolytic pathway.
source: Conversely, in immature neonatal myocardium or iPSC-CMs, ATP production is predominately through the glycolytic pathway (Sacchetto et al., 2019; Siasos et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by two citations.

claim: BNP is expressed in iPSC-CMs, which secrete the hormone into their culture media.
source: BNP is also expressed in iPSC-CMs, which secrete the hormone into their culture media.
evidence: This is a statement about the biological properties of iPSC-CMs.

claim: During heart failure, BNP secretions are elevated.
source: During heart failure, BNP secretions are elevated (Bay et al., 2003; Doust et al., 2006; Januzzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by three citations.

claim: Cardiomyocytes in the adult human heart contain approximately 30% mitochondria by cell volume.
source: Cardiomyocytes in the adult human heart contain approximately 30% mitochondria by cell volume.
evidence: This is a statement about established biological knowledge.

claim: Mitochondria critically regulate many cellular processes, such as metabolism, oxidative stress, cell survival, and apoptotic death.
source: These mitochondria critically regulate many cellular processes, such as metabolism, oxidative stress, cell survival, and apoptotic death (Ventura-Clapier et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ventura-Clapier et al., 2011.

claim: Exposing iPSC-CMs to various clinically approved compounds with known cardiotoxicities led to a dose-dependent decrease in mitochondrial function in these cells.
source: In previous studies, exposing iPSC-CMs to various clinically approved compounds with known cardiotoxicities led to a dose-dependent decrease in mitochondrial function in these cells (Burridge et al., 2016; Rana et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by two citations.

claim: Deep neural networks significantly outperformed random forest by 22–27% in four measured metrics.
source: Another advantage of deep learning is that deep neural networks significantly outperformed random forest by 22–27% in four measured metrics (Idakwo et al., 2019), suggesting that this approach is more robust than traditional chemoinformatics analysis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Idakwo et al., 2019.

claim: The Z-factor is a statistical measure of assay variability and reproducibility.
source: The Z-factor is a statistical measure of assay variability and reproducibility (Zhang et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 1999.

claim: A Z-factor of 0.5 is an acceptable level for an HCS in cell-based assays.
source: For example, a minimum number of 1500 iPSC-CMs per well of a 384-well plate was required to reach a Z-factor of approximately 0.5, which is an acceptable level for an HCS in cell-based assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement about established standards in high-content screening.

claim: A minimum de facto cutoff of 0.5 for Z-factor is used in HTS.
source: In this case, the associated Z-factors are far lower than a minimum de facto cutoff of 0.5 for HTS (Bray and Carpenter, 2017; Zhang et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by two citations.

claim: The screening approach can be used during target discovery and lead optimization to de-risk early-stage drug discovery.
source: By using this screening approach during target discovery and lead optimization, we can de-risk early-stage drug discovery.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential application of the screening approach.

claim: Combining deep learning with iPSC technology is an effective way to interrogate cellular phenotypes and identify drugs that may protect against diseased phenotypes and deleterious mutations.
source: We show that the broad applicability of combining deep learning with iPSC technology is an effective way to interrogate cellular phenotypes and identify drugs that may protect against diseased phenotypes and deleterious mutations.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the abstract about the overall findings of the study.

claim: Deep learning is a highly sensitive method to detect cardiotoxicity phenotypes that are undetectable by traditional single-readout assays.
source: Our findings support that deep learning is a highly sensitive method to detect cardiotoxicity phenotypes that are undetectable by traditional single-readout assays.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of deep learning and immunostaining readouts.

claim: The screening strategy is cell and modality agnostic, and it can be applied to a range of indications, such as orphan and neglected diseases.
source: Our screening strategy is cell and modality agnostic, and it can be applied to a range of indications, such as orphan and neglected diseases.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applicability of the screening strategy.

claim: Combining iPSC technology and deep learning can accelerate discovery efforts by supporting rapid model development and interrogation of targets that could be used in different areas of research and for multiple indications.
source: Thus, combining iPSC technology and deep learning can accelerate discovery efforts by supporting rapid model development and interrogation of targets that could be used in different areas of research and for multiple indications.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the potential impact of the approach.

claim: The library of diverse compounds was sourced from Enamine and screened at 1.0 μM.
source: The library of diverse compounds was sourced from Enamine (Kyiv, Ukraine) and screened at 1.0 μM.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for screening the diverse compound library.

claim: The bioactive compound library was sourced from Selleck Chemicals and screened at three doses of 0.3 μM, 1.0 μM, and 3.0 μM in 0.1% DMSO.
source: A library containing 1280 bioactive compounds consisting of FDA-approved drugs, tool compounds, and pre-clinical drug candidates was sourced from Selleck Chemicals (Houston, TX). Screening and validation studies on the bioactive compounds were performed at three doses of 0.3 μM, 1.0 μM, and 3.0 μM in 0.1% DMSO.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for screening the bioactive compound library.

claim: iPSCs were differentiated into iPSC-CMs using the Wnt modulation-differentiation method with 7 μM CHIR and 5 μM IWP2.
source: iPSCs were differentiated into iPSC-CMs using the Wnt modulation-differentiation method (Lian et al., 2012) with 7 μM CHIR (Selleckchem) and 5 μM IWP2 (Sigma) in RPMI media supplemented with B27 (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for differentiating iPSCs into iPSC-CMs, supported by a citation to Lian et al., 2012.

claim: iPSC-CMs were purified using 1 μM blasticidin.
source: iPSC-CMs were purified using 1 μM blasticidin (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for purifying iPSC-CMs.

claim: iPSC-CMs were thawed in RPMI with B27% and 10% FBS directly onto Matrigel-coated 384-well plates at a density of 20,000 cells/well.
source: iPSC-CMs were thawed in RPMI with B27% and 10% FBS directly onto Matrigel-coated 384-well plates at a density of 20,000 cells/well.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for thawing and plating iPSC-CMs.

claim: TCM media comprises DMEM without glucose, 10% dialyzed FBS, 10 mM D-(+)-galactose, and 1 mM sodium pyruvate.
source: TCM media comprises Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) without glucose, 10% dialyzed FBS, 10 mM D-(+)-galactose, and 1 mM sodium pyruvate.
evidence: This describes the composition of TCM media.

claim: Sarcomere organization and alignment were assessed using SGFT with a pattern size of 1.8, scanning resolution of 16, and a Fourier threshold of >0.8.
source: Sarcomere organization and alignment were assessed using scanning gradient Fourier transform (SGFT) with a pattern size of 1.8, scanning resolution of 16, and a Fourier threshold of >0.8 (Salick et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for assessing sarcomere organization, supported by a citation to Salick et al., 2020.

claim: Deep learning artificial intelligence models were built using the PhenoLearn platform.
source: Deep learning artificial intelligence models were built using the PhenoLearn platform (https://www.phenolearn.com/).
evidence: This describes the platform used for building deep learning models.

claim: A ResNet50 architecture, a 50-layer-deep convolutional neural network, was used for the deep learning models.
source: We used PyTorch as the framework for the deep learning library, and a ResNet50 architecture, a 50-layer-deep convolutional neural network.
evidence: This describes the neural network architecture used for the deep learning models.

claim: 80% of the images were used to construct the neural network and the remaining 20% to validate the deep learning model.
source: We used 80% of the images to construct the neural network and the remaining 20% to validate the deep learning model.
evidence: This describes the data split used for training and validating the deep learning models.

claim: A consistent set of parameters were used for all training operations, including an initial learning rate of 0.01 and 20 epochs.
source: A consistent set of parameters were used for all training operations, including an initial learning rate of 0.01 and 20 epochs.
evidence: This describes the training parameters used for the deep learning models.

claim: RNA-seq data was deposited on the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database with accession number GSE172181.
source: We deposited our RNA-seq data on the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database: GEO Submission (GSE172181), https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE172181.
evidence: This describes the data deposition for the RNA-seq data.

claim: The Agilent Seahorse XFe96 Analyzer was used to measure mitochondrial function in iPSC-CMs.
source: The Agilent Seahorse XFe96 Analyzer was used to measure mitochondrial function in iPSC-CMs.
evidence: This describes the instrument used for measuring mitochondrial function.

claim: WTC iPSC-CMs were seeded at 30,000 cells per XFe96 well and recovered in TCM media for 1 week.
source: WTC iPSC-CMs were seeded at 30,000 cells per XFe96 well and recovered in TCM media for 1 week.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for seeding and recovering iPSC-CMs for the Seahorse assay.

claim: Cardiotoxic compounds were diluted to 3 µM, 1 µM, 0.3 µM, and 0.1 µM in 1.0% DMSO in TCM media and administered in fresh media for 4 days.
source: Cardiotoxic compounds were diluted to 3 µM, 1 µM, 0.3 µM, and 0.1 µM in 1.0% DMSO in TCM media. Drugs were administered in fresh media for 4 days.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for treating iPSC-CMs with cardiotoxic compounds.

claim: The Mito Stress Test was performed with inhibitors injected in the following order: oligomycin (2.5 µM), FCCP (1 µM), and rotenone and antimycin A (0.5 µM).
source: Next, the Mito Stress Test was performed with inhibitors injected in the following order: oligomycin (2.5 µM), carbonyl cyanide 4-(trifluoromethoxy) phenylhydrazone (FCCP; 1 µM), and rotenone and antimycin A (0.5 µM).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for the Mito Stress Test.

claim: OCR values were normalized to the total nuclear count per well as quantified by Hoechst staining.
source: OCR values were normalized to the total nuclear count per well as quantified by Hoechst staining.
evidence: This describes the normalization method for OCR values.

claim: Proteasome activity was measured in iPSC-CMs using the Proteasome-Glo Chymotrypsin-Like Assay.
source: Proteasome activity was measured in iPSC-CMs using the Proteasome-Glo Chymotrypsin-Like Assay according to the manufacturer's instructions (Promega).
evidence: This describes the assay used for measuring proteasome activity.

claim: Cells were incubated with the proteasome inhibitors (ranging from 2 to 5000 nM) for 1 hr before running the proteasome activity assay.
source: Cells were incubated with the inhibitors (ranging from 2 to 5000 nM) for 1 hr before running the assay.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for the proteasome activity assay.

claim: IC50s for proteasome inhibitors were calculated using PRISM 8 software.
source: IC50s were calculated using PRISM 8 software.
evidence: This describes the software used for calculating IC50s.

claim: The proBNP/NPPB human sandwich ELISA kit was used to determine the level of secreted human proBNP.
source: The proBNP/NPPB human sandwich ELISA kit (Invitrogen) was used to determine the level of secreted human proBNP.
evidence: This describes the assay used for measuring proBNP levels.

claim: Cell culture media was collected from wells containing approximately 105 iPSC-CMs exposed to cardiotoxic drugs for 4 days.
source: Cell culture media was collected from wells containing approximately 105 iPSC-CMs exposed to cardiotoxic drugs for 4 days.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for collecting media for the proBNP assay.

claim: Raw RNA-seq reads were aligned with Salmon (version 1.3.0) to the GENCODE version 33 reference transcript assembly (hg38 v.13).
source: Raw RNA-seq reads were aligned with Salmon (Patro et al., 2017) (version 1.3.0) to the GENCODE (Frankish et al., 2019) version 33 reference transcript assembly (hg38 v.13) using best practice parameters to ensure mapping validity and reproducibility (--seqBias --gcBias --posBias --useVBOpt --rangeFactorizationBins 4 --validateMappings --mimicStrictBT2).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics method for aligning RNA-seq reads, supported by citations to Salmon and GENCODE.

claim: tximport was used to generate an expression matrix normalized to transcripts per million (TPM).
source: Next, tximport (Soneson et al., 2015) was used to generate an expression matrix normalized to transcripts per million (TPM).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics method for generating the expression matrix, supported by a citation to tximport.

claim: Protein-coding genes were determined using Ensembl release 100 human annotation (GRCh38, Apr 2020) and extracted by biomaRt (version 2.45.9).
source: Protein-coding genes were determined using Ensembl release 100 human annotation (Cunningham et al., 2019) (GRCh38, Apr 2020) and extracted by biomaRt (Durinck et al., 2009) (version 2.45.9); non-protein-coding and mitochondrial genes were omitted from the analysis.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics method for determining protein-coding genes, supported by citations to Ensembl and biomaRt.

claim: PCA models were generated in the R environment using the prcomp function.
source: For the initial assessment, principal component analysis (PCA) models were generated in the R environment using the prcomp function, and the first two principal components were used for visualization.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics method for generating PCA models.

claim: Euclidean distance in the PCA space was calculated using the pca2euclid function from the tcR package.
source: To quantify the distances between each drug's samples and generate a PCA-based similarity matrix, we used Euclidean distance in the PCA space, as calculated by the pca2euclid function from the tcR package.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics method for calculating distances in PCA space.
